cim: Emomali Rahmon calls for preventing terrorists from using artificial intelligence - Азия-Плюс
cim_eredeti: Emomali Rahmon calls for preventing terrorists from using artificial intelligence - Азия-Плюс
szoveg_eredeti:
Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon has proposed establishing cooperation between the “Aqaba Process” and the “Dushanbe Process” to counter new threats linked to the development of artificial intelligence. He made the proposal on November 6 at the Aqaba Process meeting on AI security in Astana.

According to Rahmon, the rapid development of artificial intelligence is opening new opportunities for the economy, science, education and public administration, while at the same time creating additional security risks.

The president noted that the use of modern technologies by terrorist and extremist organizations is a particular cause for concern.

Rahmon stated that terrorist and radical groups are already using digital technologies to spread extremist ideas, recruit supporters, influence public opinion and create disinformation.

The president stressed that Tajikistan advocates for the responsible and safe use of artificial intelligence in compliance with legal and ethical standards.

Rahmon recalled that at Tajikistan’s initiative, the UN General Assembly has adopted two resolutions related to artificial intelligence over the past two years.

One of them is dedicated to the role of AI in creating new opportunities for sustainable development in Central Asia. The initiative provides for using the potential of the Artificial Intelligence Center in Dushanbe as a regional platform for cooperation.

This includes, in particular, training AI security specialists, developing recommendations on risk assessment and the prevention of cyber threats.

The other resolution establishes August 31 as the International Day of Safe, Secure and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence. According to Rahmon, these initiatives should help shape common approaches to the use of new technologies.

Speaking about countering digital threats, the president noted the need to strengthen national cybersecurity systems, international cooperation and the prompt exchange of information.

In this context, he described the “Dushanbe Process on Combating Terrorism and Its Financing” as an important platform for interaction between states and international organizations.

Rahmon believes that cooperation between the “Dushanbe Process” and the “Aqaba Process” will make it possible to share practical experience, develop joint approaches and strengthen countries’ capacity to counter new threats.

He identified four priority areas: developing international cooperation on the safe use of AI and preventing its use for terrorist purposes; strengthening interaction between law enforcement agencies and security services; building institutional capacity and training specialists; and improving digital literacy among young people and countering the spread of extremist ideas online.

In the president’s view, implementing these measures will help improve the effectiveness of joint efforts to combat terrorism, extremism and transnational organized crime.

Business representatives from the two countries signed 25 documents worth a total of $2.5 billion.
